training.intro: Each run learns from approved replies and datasets, and adds a new version. The version stores only what changed.

learns.title: What training learns from
learns.label: Approved replies
learns.what: Approved replies count, edited ones included. A reply left out of training in Chat isn't counted.

views.label: Show
views.examplesNote: Each example is a conversation as it goes into training. The highlighted reply is the one the model learns.

form.title: Train a new version
form.intro: Choose what the run learns from, then start it. Only one run trains at a time.
form.name: Name of the new version
form.nameHint: Optional. Without a name, the version shows only its number.

startsFrom.label: Start from
startsFrom.base: The base model has no earlier training. The new version learns only from the examples.
startsFrom.enhance: Building on {version} keeps what it learned and adds the new examples.

form.useCorrectionsHint: Replies approved in Chat, edited ones included. Approved replies: {count}
form.activate: Make it the active version when done
form.activateHint: Chat then uses the new version. An older version can be made active again.
form.expertChanged: Some expert settings have been changed and apply to this run.
form.custom: Custom value: {value}. Set in Expert mode.
form.loadingPlan: Loading the settings for this machine
form.noModel: This project has no model yet. A new version can be trained once its first run has finished.

blocked.noReplies: There is nothing to learn from yet. Approve a reply in Chat or choose a dataset.
blocked.noSource: Turn on learning from the approved replies or choose a dataset.
blocked.settings: Some settings need a different value.

epochs.label: Passes over the examples
epochs.hint: How many times the model goes through all the examples. More passes learn more, but the model can start to memorize them.

rank.label: How much the model may change
rank.hint: A larger change can learn more. It needs more memory and disk space.

rate.label: How strongly it learns
rate.hint: A strong rate learns fast and can overshoot. A gentle rate is slow and steady.

datasets.label: Datasets from the library
datasets.limitHint: Leave empty to use all rows.

expert.intro: Every setting a run takes. The defaults suit this machine and model.
expert.epochsHint: Passes over all the examples. Maximum steps overrides it.
expert.rankHint: Size of the add-on. A larger rank can learn more.
expert.maxStepsHint: Stops after this many steps. Leave empty to run every pass in full.
expert.maxSeqLenHint: Longer examples are skipped. Memory use grows with this.
expert.batchSizeHint: Examples processed together. A larger batch needs more memory.
expert.gradAccumHint: Batches collected before each update. The effective batch is the batch size times this.
expert.loraAlphaHint: Scales the effect of the add-on. Often twice the rank.
expert.loraDropoutHint: Share of the add-on skipped at random while training. 0 turns it off.
expert.rsloraHint: Scales by the square root of the rank. Keeps large ranks stable.
expert.biasesHint: Also changes the model's bias values. The version can then only be exported as a merged model.
expert.quantizeHint: Loads the base model compressed to 4 bits. Needs less memory. Quality drops slightly.
expert.checkpointingHint: Recomputes some work to save memory. Training is slower.

problem.limit: Enter a whole number of 1 or more.

verdict.unknown: Whether this machine can train this model isn't known.

loss.explain: How far the model's answer is from the reply in the example. Lower is better. It falls as the model learns.

epoch.explain: One full pass over all the examples. With two epochs the model sees every example twice.

learning_rate.explain: How big a step the model takes each time it learns. A high rate learns fast but can overshoot. A low rate is slow and steady.

adamw_torch.explain: The usual way of adjusting a model while it trains. It keeps two extra numbers for every parameter, so it needs more memory than the model itself.

adamw_8bit.explain: AdamW with its extra numbers stored in 8 bits. It needs less memory.
